title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
spaceBreakdown:
- recursion call-stack depth: up to h (tree height), worst case O(n) for skewed tree, O(log n) for balanced
- no containers or arrays allocated
- not counted: input tree, returned node
approach: The LCA is the node where p and q diverge into different subtrees, or where one of them is the node itself. Recurse on both children: if the current node is null, p, or q, return it immediately. If both children return non-null, the current node is the LCA. Otherwise, propagate the non-null child upward. This works because the first node where both p and q are found in different subtrees (or one is the node itself) is the lowest common ancestor.
hints: What property must the LCA node satisfy regarding where p and q are located relative to it? The tree has up to 10^5 nodes, so visiting each node once is affordable.
Use recursive depth-first search. In Example 1, at node 3 the left subtree returns node 5 and the right returns node 1; since both are non-null, node 3 is the LCA.

**Smallest input** - only two nodes, root is one of the targets
`Input: root = [1,2], p = 1, q = 2` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: not checking `root == p || root == q` before recursing into children → returns 2

**Both in different subtrees** - LCA is an internal node with one target per child
`Input: root = [3,5,1,6,2,0,8,null,null,7,4], p = 5, q = 1` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: returning the left result immediately when non-null, before checking the right subtree → returns 5

**p is ancestor of q** - a node is its own descendant per the definition
`Input: root = [3,5,1,6,2,0,8,null,null,7,4], p = 5, q = 4` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: returning NULL when only one child subtree yields a match, instead of propagating that result upward → returns NULL

**Non-BST tree** - value ordering does not reflect tree structure
`Input: root = [3,5,1,6,2,0,8,null,null,7,4], p = 6, q = 4` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: using BST-style value comparison to decide which child to visit → returns NULL

followUps.q: What if you need to answer many LCA queries on the same tree?
followUps.a: Preprocess the tree with binary lifting: store each node's 2^k-th ancestor for all k up to log n. Each query then brings both nodes to the same depth and jumps them up together in O(log n). Preprocessing is O(n log n) time and space.

followUps.q: What if each node has a parent pointer but no child pointers?
followUps.a: Walk from p up to the root, storing every ancestor in a hash set. Then walk from q upward; the first ancestor already in the set is the LCA. This takes O(h) time and O(h) space, where h is the tree height.

followUps.q: What if p or q might not exist in the tree?
followUps.a: Modify the recursion to return a count of how many of p and q were found alongside the candidate node. Only return a non-null LCA when the count reaches 2. The time and space complexity remain O(n) and O(h) respectively.
